ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $AC$ is the tangent of $\odot O$ with $A$ being the point of tangency, and $BC$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $D$. Connect $OD$. If $\angle C=50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AC$ is the tangent to the circle $\odot O$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAB=90^\circ$,\\
And since $\angle C=50^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=90^\circ-50^\circ=40^\circ$,\\
And since $OD=OB$,\\
$\therefore \angle BDO=\angle ABC=40^\circ$,\\
And since $\angle AOD=\angle OBD+\angle OBD$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOD=40^\circ+40^\circ=\boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter passing through the center O of the circle, A is on the circle on the left side, and B is on the circle on the right side; AC is the vertical tangent through point A; from C to B there is an oblique line, the oblique line intersects the circle at D, and C, D, B are collinear; OD is also connected in the figure. Reasoning: Because AC is the tangent to the circle at point A, and OA and AB are on the same straight line, the tangent AC is perpendicular to the radius OA, that is, ∠CAB = 90°. It is known that ∠C = 50°, so in right triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 90° - 50° = 40°. Since O is on AB and D is on BC, ∠OBD and ∠ABC are angles formed in the same direction, so ∠OBD = 40°. Also because OB and OD are both radii of the circle, OB = OD, triangle OBD is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠ODB = 40°, and thus ∠BOD = 180° - 40° - 40° = 100°. Because A, O, B are collinear, ∠AOB is a straight angle, so ∠AOD = 180° - ∠BOD = 180° - 100° = 80°.
